cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to Israel in the valley opposite Beth-peor. Now he gets to the point: listen up, Israel. That's the original "Hey. Put the phone DOWN. Look at me."

cards.question: Moses is teaching Israel statutes and ordinances to follow. Why, according to him?

answers.text: So they may live and take the land
So they may earn back their freedom
So they may keep Moses as leader

cards.question: Moses says Israel can add a few good rules of their own to the commands he's giving them.

cards.text: Then Moses points to something they saw with their own eyes: Baal-peor. Everyone who followed Baal of Peor, the LORD destroyed from among them.

cards.question: And the people who held fast to the LORD at Baal-peor? What does Moses say about them?

answers.text: Every one of them is alive today
Most of them lost their homes
They were sent back to Egypt

cards.text: Moses has taught them the statutes just as the LORD commanded him, so they can follow them in the land. And keeping them, he says, gets NOTICED, like a fresh batch in the oven: you never have to announce it, the whole block just knows.

cards.question: When other peoples hear about all of Israel's statutes, what does Moses say they'll say?

answers.text: This great nation is wise and understanding
This great nation is strict and stubborn
This great nation is fierce and fearless

cards.question: Moses asks: what nation is great enough to have a god as ___ to them as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on Him?

cards.text: Then a second question: what nation has statutes and ordinances as righteous as this whole law he's setting before them today? Two questions in a row, and the answer to both is NOBODY.
But, Moses says, be on your guard and diligently watch yourselves. That's me with a batch in the oven: I'm not leaving, I'm not blinking, I am PRESSED against the glass.

cards.question: What does Moses warn Israel not to let slip from their hearts?

answers.text: The things their eyes have seen
The promises they made to Moses

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to keep the things they've seen just between themselves.

cards.text: Then he takes them back to the day they stood before the LORD at Horeb. The LORD told Moses to gather the people to hear His words, so they'd learn to fear Him and teach their children.

cards.question: The people came near and stood at the base of the mountain at Horeb. What was the mountain like?

answers.text: Blazing with fire up to the heavens
Wrapped in a soft white mist
Quiet and green in the sunshine

cards.text: Black clouds, deep darkness, and the LORD spoke to them out of the fire. They heard the sound of the words.

cards.question: When the LORD spoke to Israel out of the fire at Horeb, they saw His form.

cards.text: There was only a voice. And that voice declared His covenant, which He commanded them to follow.

cards.question: The LORD wrote His covenant on two tablets of stone: the Ten ___.

cards.text: At that time, the LORD also commanded Moses to teach them the statutes for the land across the Jordan. Now Moses circles back to Horeb, where they saw no form of any kind.

cards.question: Since Israel saw no form at Horeb, what does Moses warn them not to make for themselves?

answers.text: An idol of any form or shape
An altar out of cut stones

cards.question: Moses says an idol shaped like a bird or a fish is fine, as long as it isn't shaped like a person.

cards.text: Then Moses talks about looking up at the sun, the moon and the stars, all the host of heaven. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer with ZERO sky, so believe me, I understand looking up there with your mouth hanging open.

cards.question: Moses says Israel may bow down to the sun, moon and stars, as long as they also worship the LORD.

cards.text: Yet the LORD took them and brought them out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt. Iron furnace, friend. I've stood next to an oven my whole life, and I would NOT want to be inside one.

cards.question: Out of the iron furnace of Egypt, what did the LORD bring Israel out to be?

cards.text: Then Moses gets personal. The LORD was angry with him on account of them and swore he would not cross the Jordan, and Moses says he won't be crossing, because he must die in this land.

cards.question: Even though Moses won't cross the Jordan, he says the people will still cross over and take possession of that good land.

cards.text: So be careful, Moses says. Don't forget the covenant the LORD made with them, and don't make an idol in the form of anything He has forbidden.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD your God is a consuming ___, a jealous God.

cards.text: Then Moses looks way down the road, after they've had children and grandchildren and been in the land a long time. What if they act corruptly then and make an idol, provoking the LORD to anger?
Moses calls heaven and earth as witnesses against them, this day. Friend, when heaven and earth are BOTH on the witness list, you do not want to be on the other side of that case.

cards.question: If they turn to idols, Moses says they would still live long in the land they're crossing the Jordan to possess.
If Israel turned to idols, what does Moses say the LORD would do with them next?
Once they're scattered, Moses says only a few of them would survive among the nations.

cards.text: And there they'd serve man-made gods of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell. A god that can't even smell a fresh batch of chocolate chip? Friend, I'm a COOKIE STAMPER, and I've got more going on than that.

cards.question: Even scattered among the nations, Moses says, if they seek the LORD they will find Him. How do they need to seek Him?

answers.text: With all their heart and soul
With offerings of silver and gold
With a journey back to Horeb

cards.text: When they're in distress and all these things have happened, then in later days they'll return to the LORD their God and listen to His voice.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD will not abandon them or forget the covenant with their fathers, because the LORD your God is a ___ God.

cards.text: Go ahead, Moses says, ask from one end of the heavens to the other, all the way back to the day God created man: "Has anything as great as this ever happened or been reported?" Search it, search it again, refresh the page, you are NOT gonna find it.

cards.question: What does Moses say no other people has ever done the way Israel has?

answers.text: Heard God's voice from the fire and lived
Seen God's face on a mountain and lived
Walked straight through a fire and lived

cards.text: Or has any god ever tried to take a nation out of another nation by trials, signs, wonders and war, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm? That's exactly what the LORD did for them in Egypt, right before their eyes.

cards.question: Why does Moses say Israel was shown all these things?

answers.text: So they'd know the LORD alone is God
So they'd know they were stronger than Egypt
So they'd know Moses was a great leader

cards.text: He let them hear His voice from heaven to discipline them. And on earth He showed them His great fire, and they heard His words out of it.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD chose Israel because they were greater and mightier than the other nations.

cards.text: It was because He loved their fathers, and He brought them out of Egypt by His presence and great power. He did it to drive out nations greater and mightier than them, and to give them their land for an inheritance.

cards.question: Moses says the LORD is God in heaven above, but other gods rule the earth below.

cards.text: Then Moses brings the whole sermon home: keep His statutes and commandments, which he's giving them today. He STICKS the landing, friend, while I start one story about the drawer and twenty minutes later I'm still describing the rubber bands I shared it with.

cards.question: Why does Moses say to keep the LORD's statutes and commandments?

answers.text: So they and their children may prosper in the land
So they may win every battle without a fight
So Moses might cross the Jordan after all
